Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

effort noun

an attempt

also attempt, in an effort to, a vain attempt, endeavour, undertaking

classical

Caes. BG 1.8.4: hōc cōnātū dēstitērunt
Verg. A. 12.910–911: in mediīs cōnātibus aegrī succidimus

cōnātus, cōnātūs m.

noun, fourth declension · Declension on Wiktionary

an attempt, an undertaking; an effort

Lewis & Short: “an attempt, effort, undertaking, enterprise, endeavor”; in the plural, efforts: multīs frūstrā cōnātibus captīs, after many vain attempts (Liv. 3.5.6, Lewis & Short). The verb is cōnārī (see try).

Other words

  • cōnātum, cōnātī n. — an attempt; usually plural, cōnāta, what one has set out to do

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.3.6: perfacile factū esse illīs probat cōnāta perficere · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • sī perrumpere possent cōnātī, operis mūnītiōne et mīlitum concursū et tēlīs repulsī, hōc cōnātū dēstitērunt

    they tried to see if they could break through, but were driven back by the earthworks, the soldiers’ charge and missiles, and gave up the attemptCaes. BG 1.8.4

  • ac velut in somnīs, oculōs ubi languida pressit nocte quiēs, nēquīquam avidōs extendere cursūs velle vidēmur et in mediīs cōnātibus aegrī succidimus

    and as in dreams, when at night drowsy rest has closed our eyes, we seem to want, in vain, to run on eagerly, and in the middle of our efforts we sink down, exhaustedVerg. A. 12.908–912

See also try, effort.
